title: Characteristic-zero log-stratum independence of induced resolution towers
statement:
There exists a normalized desingularization algorithm $\mathcal F$ on reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent schemes over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-exc-excellent-ring]. It assigns a finite tower of ordinary blowups followed by normalization, retaining the defining ideal of every center [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-sc-normalization], with regular last scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. It is functorial for regular morphisms, meaning flat morphisms with geometrically regular fibres: the source tower is the contracted pullback of the target tower, with ordered extended center ideals, compatibly with identities and composition. Contraction removes unit-center isomorphism stages. The rule is defined on finite disjoint unions as well.

Fix any such algorithm. Restrict it to rational toric realizations, descend its torus-invariant centers to monoschemes and then sharpen to fans as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. The result is a saturated desingularization $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ of fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers, smooth-functorial in the sense of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]: each $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}(F)$ is a finite tower of saturated blowups along nonempty coherent monoid ideals with smooth last fan, and for a smooth morphism $g:G\to F$, $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}(G)$ is canonically the contraction of $g^*\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}(F)$, retaining the centers and their order, compatibly with composition, open localizations, isomorphisms and inclusions into finite disjoint unions. No center of $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}(F)$ is the whole monoid sheaf. On a Noetherian fs log regular scheme $(V,M)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], whose characteristic group completions are torsion free because its characteristic monoids are fs and sharp, $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ induces a finite saturated log blowup tower: on strict etale neighbourhoods with fan charts it is the pullback of $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ of the fan, contracted, and these local towers glue by strict etale descent [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup], [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent]. No log center of this tower is the whole log structure. Write $T_{\mathcal F}(V,M)$ for its underlying normalized blowup tower, whose center ideals are the ideals $\alpha(\mathcal I)\mathcal O$ generated by the log centers $\mathcal I$; hence every center of $T_{\mathcal F}(V,M)$ has nonempty zero locus. Let $(V,M)$ and $(W,N)$ be Noetherian separated fs log regular schemes, and let $\phi:W\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ be an isomorphism of their underlying schemes. Assume that every generic point of every log stratum for either log structure has residue characteristic zero. The strata are the connected components of the constant-rank loci of the group completions of the characteristic monoids. Then
$$T_{\mathcal F}(W,N)=\phi^*T_{\mathcal F}(V,M).$$
This equality identifies all stages in their original order and all defining center ideals, without separately contracting the towers on the connected components. It applies to finite disjoint unions, including the empty scheme. No quasi-excellence hypothesis on $V$ or $W$ is required.

source.place: VIII Theorem 2.3.10 and Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.12, pp.93--94 (existence and normalized regular functoriality); 3.2.19 and Theorem 3.4.15 with its proof and Remark 3.4.16(i), pp.106,113--114 (induced rule, independence, and synchronization); 2.3.2 (nonempty centers), 3.1.27, 3.2.20 and Remark 3.2.21, p.106 (smooth-functorial fan rule), 3.3.15, pp.109--110 (induced log tower as a contraction).

proof.text: Choose the ordinary regular-functorial rule $F$ of [lem-per-qe-ordinary-regular-resolution]. On normal inputs let $N$ assign the normalized towers of [lem-per-normalized-tower-regular-pullback]: they have coherent centers with nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes and regular last level, and regular base change supplies the comparisons. For a regular $h:T\to S$ of normal inputs every stage of the pulled-back normalized tower is normal (the source is normal and later stages are normalizations), so a unit-ideal stage is an identity and the ordinary deletions correspond exactly to deleting these identities; identity/composition laws and surjective nondeletion survive. This fails for nonnormal sources: if the first center of $F(X)$ misses a nonnormal point of an open $Y\subset X$, the pulled-back unit stage is $Y^\nu\to Y$, not an isomorphism, so the normalization of $F$ itself is not regular-functorial in the stated sense. Therefore let $\mathcal F=H_N$ of [lem-per-qe-conductor-normalized-resolution-extension]: first the normalized blowup of the conductor ideal, whose zero set is exactly the nonnormal locus and which commutes with regular base change, then $N$. That lemma gives the finite centered tower, regular last level, nonempty nowhere dense centers, contracted-pullback comparisons deleting only unit stages, which are isomorphisms, identity/composition laws, finite disjoint unions and the empty input. This proves the existence assertion.

For the remaining assertions fix any normalized rule $\mathcal F$ as in the statement, using the convention of VIII 2.3.2 that a normalized desingularization tower has nonempty nowhere dense centers. Reduced finite-type rational schemes are excellent, hence qe, by [lem-exc-fields-excellent] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] applied on affine charts. Its restriction to them is smooth-functorial: smooth maps are flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], their fibres are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], and those fibres are geometrically regular by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. Toric realizations belong to this domain by [lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-functorial-tower-torus-equivariance] to each component torus, extended by the identity on the other components. It supplies torus invariance of every actual center ideal and of the whole centered tower, with no contractions for the surjective projection and action maps.

For each toric realization, [lem-trf-monoscheme-toric-tower-descent] descends its centered tower uniquely to monoschemes, with smooth last monoscheme. Apply [lem-trf-monoscheme-tower-comparison-coherence]: the comparisons of the fixed $\mathcal F$ meet its smooth-pullback and identity/composition hypotheses, and the preceding descent gives its unique lifts. Then apply the rule bijection in [lem-trf-sharpening-fan-bijection] on the subcategory with torsion-free sharp stalk groups. This constructs the specified $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ on all fine torsion-free fans. It retains the centers, order, smooth last object and coherent comparisons. The nonempty zero scheme of each toric center excludes the unit monoid ideal; the ideal correspondence and sharpening preserve that condition. Open localizations, isomorphisms and component inclusions have isomorphisms on stalk monoids, so are smooth by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].

On a log scheme with a fan chart, pull back the fan tower by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup] and delete whole-monoid centers. This is independent of the chart and has strict-pullback comparisons. Indeed [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] identifies, locally at each source point, the two chart maps through isomorphic affine fan localizations. Smooth-functoriality of $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ and strict compatibility of chart pullback identify the local contracted towers. To synchronize these local identifications, use the rule on the finite disjoint union of the fan localizations; its surjective restrictions to the original fan cover retain all indices before pullback. The uniqueness of center-preserving comparisons in [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-rigidity] glues the local comparisons, with identity and composition laws. Now [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] supplies the global finite log tower. Its charted rule is precisely the one just compared and includes finite disjoint unions. This establishes the asserted strict etale construction.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15 and Remark 3.3.16, pp.109--110.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-log-blowup-regularization] to this chosen smooth-functorial fan rule. Its statement gives the normalized underlying tower, Noetherian normal log regular stages, regular last scheme, and equality of strict-transform and scheme pullback towers for strict morphisms. Its hypotheses allow our separated Noetherian inputs and require no excellence. The center is $J=\alpha(\mathcal I)\mathcal O$. No global center is the whole log structure, by contraction in the preceding step. It follows that $V(J)$ is nonempty: choose a point where the log ideal is proper; in its local ring all its generators are nonunits, for a log section maps to a unit exactly when it is a log unit [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Hence they generate a proper ring ideal there. Conversely a whole log ideal gives the unit ring ideal. This also explains why the contractions match on the log and scheme sides.

Transport $(W,N)$ along $\phi$ so that both log structures are on the single scheme $X=V$. Choose a common surjective finite strict etale cover on which both admit global charts, by refining the two covers of [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup]; take the finite disjoint union, rather than separately contracting on its components. By [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization] neither full tower loses a stage on this surjective cover. Equality with ordered ring centers can be tested on it by [lem-per-normalized-tower-support-recovery]. Thus it suffices to compare the towers when both log structures are Zariski, keeping one indexing on this whole cover.

Write $B_M=T_{\mathcal F}(X,M)$ and $B_N=T_{\mathcal F}(X,N)$. By [lem-per-log-monoidal-associated-points], their associated-point images are contained respectively in $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$ and $\operatorname{Fan}(X,N)$. Both sets lie in $X_{\mathbf Q}$ by the stratum hypothesis. The rational localization is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism; it need not be open. [lem-per-normalized-tower-support-recovery] therefore recovers each full tower by closing the centers of its uncontracted restriction to $X_{\mathbf Q}$. The strict comparison already obtained identifies the contracted restriction with the induced tower of the restricted log structure. No stage contracts: a nonempty center has an associated point, all such points map into $X_{\mathbf Q}$, and so its restriction is nonempty. Hence equality for the two towers on $X_{\mathbf Q}$ implies equality on $X$. From now on $X$ is a rational scheme, with no assumption that it is quasi-excellent.

Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ and set $\widehat X_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}}$. By [lem-trf-log-regular-completed-chart], after choosing a suitable sharp chart for $M$ its complete ring is $B_k(P,n)=k[[P]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$, with $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$ and with the same chart monomials. For $N$ it has a presentation $B_{k'}(Q,m)$; both coefficient fields map isomorphically to the same residue field, but need not be the same embedded subfield. Both contain $\mathbf Q$. Apply [lem-per-rational-toric-completion-regular-map] to each presentation. The two maps to the rational toric polynomial models are regular, and the complete scheme is a reduced Noetherian qe input for $\mathcal F$. Each completion map to its respective log scheme is strict; its underlying scheme map to $X$ is not claimed regular.

source.place: VI 1.6(i); VIII 3.4.15, second and third proof paragraphs; Remark 3.4.16(i).

proof.text: For one of these presentations put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Its fan is the sharpening of $P$; the extra polynomial variables have trivial log structure. The toric descent and sharpening in Step 3 identify the induced log resolution on $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[P]$ with $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[P])$ including their centers. Smooth-functoriality for the polynomial projection identifies the same objects on $Z$ without contraction, since that projection is surjective. The strict log comparison from Step 5 and the chart comparison from Step 4 identify the contracted pullback of $B_M$ to $\widehat X_{\bar x}$ with the induced log resolution there. On the other hand the regular model map of Step 8 and regular-functoriality identify this induced resolution with $\mathcal F(\widehat X_{\bar x})$, after contraction. Repeat with $Q,m$ for $N$. Thus both contracted completed towers equal the value of the single scheme-theoretic algorithm on the same complete scheme.

Contractions alone do not yet identify the stage order. Let $S=\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)\cup\operatorname{Fan}(X,N)$, a finite set by [lem-per-log-monoidal-associated-points], and fix any extra geometric point $\bar x$. Choose a geometric point above each $s\in S$ and let $H$ be the finite disjoint union of their completed strict local schemes and $\widehat X_{\bar x}$. Work with the two log structures pulled back to this single $H$. Every nonempty center of either tower remains nonempty on $H$: it has an associated point over some $s\in S$ by that lemma; strict localization and completion over $s$ are faithfully flat local tests, so the fibre of this center survives [lem-per-normalized-tower-support-recovery]. Therefore neither full pullback contracts any stage. Step 9, applied simultaneously to the finite disjoint union of the respective rational toric models, identifies both full pullbacks with $\mathcal F(H)$, with actual ordered centers. The use of $\mathcal F(H)$, rather than independently chosen component towers, is essential.

Restrict the equality on $H$ to its designated summand $\widehat X_{\bar x}$ without deleting any stage. Since $\bar x$ was arbitrary, the completed strict local tests of [lem-per-normalized-tower-support-recovery] give $B_M=B_N$ with the same finite index set and all ideal centers. Step 7 recovers this equality before rational localization, and Step 6 descends it from the common strict etale cover. Undoing transport along $\phi$ gives $T_{\mathcal F}(W,N)=\phi^*T_{\mathcal F}(V,M)$. All finite unions in the argument were treated as single inputs, so this is equality with the original order, not componentwise contracted equality. On the empty scheme the contracted tower has no proper center and length zero. No step applied $\mathcal F$ directly to the possibly non-qe scheme $X$; only toric models and complete local schemes were its inputs.
